q-37341.name: Question 1
q-37341.problem: Evaluate the gradient of $g(x,y)$ at the point $({e}^{2},1)$ if $g(x,y)=(x+y)(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2}).$
q-37341.worked_solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x+y)(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2})) \\  & =1\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2})+(x+y)\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2}+1+\frac{y}{x} \\ {g}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((x+y)(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2})) \\  & =1\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2})+(x+y)\cdot (-2y) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2}-2xy-2{y}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x-3{y}^{2}-2xy\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the gradient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y) & =⟨{g}_{x}(x,y),\,{g}_{y}(x,y)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2}+1+\frac{y}{x},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡x-3{y}^{2}-2xy⟩ \\ ∇g({e}^{2},1) & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})-{1}^{2}+1+\frac{1}{{e}^{2}},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})-3\cdot {1}^{2}-2\cdot {e}^{2}\cdot 1⟩ \\  & =⟨2+{e}^{-2},-1-2{e}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

q-37341.html:
Question 1
?

Evaluate the gradient of g(x,y) at the point (e2,1) if g(x,y)=(x+y)(ln⁡x−y2).

a
 ⟨e−2,1−2e2⟩
b
 ⟨2+e−2,−1−2e2⟩
c
 ⟨2+e−2,2e2⟩
d
 ⟨2+e2,1+2e2⟩
e
 ⟨2+e2,−1−2e−2⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the partial derivatives gx(x,y)=∂∂x((x+y)(ln⁡x−y2))=1⋅(ln⁡x−y2)+(x+y)⋅1x=ln⁡x−y2+1+yxgy(x,y)=∂∂y((x+y)(ln⁡x−y2))=1⋅(ln⁡x−y2)+(x+y)⋅(−2y)=ln⁡x−y2−2xy−2y2=ln⁡x−3y2−2xy

Hence, the gradient is ∇g(x,y)=⟨gx(x,y),gy(x,y)⟩=⟨ln⁡x−y2+1+yx,ln⁡x−3y2−2xy⟩∇g(e2,1)=⟨ln⁡(e2)−12+1+1e2,ln⁡(e2)−3⋅12−2⋅e2⋅1⟩=⟨2+e−2,−1−2e2⟩

q-127649.name: Question 2
q-127649.worked_solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{y}{x}{e}^{x/y}) \\  & =(-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{y}{x}\cdot \frac{1}{y}){e}^{x/y} \\  & =\frac{x-y}{{x}^{2}}{e}^{x/y} \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{y}{x}{e}^{x/y}) \\  & =(\frac{1}{x}-\frac{y}{x}\cdot \frac{x}{{y}^{2}}){e}^{x/y} \\  & =\frac{y-x}{xy}{e}^{x/y}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\text{ }i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\text{ }j \\  & =\frac{x-y}{{x}^{2}}{e}^{x/y}\text{ }i+\frac{y-x}{xy}{e}^{x/y}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

If f(x,y)=yxex/y, find ∇f(x,y).

a
 x2−y2x2ex/yi+y2−x2xyex/yj
b
 x−yx2ex/yi+y−xxyex/yj
c
 1−y2x2yex/yi+x2−1xy2ex/yj
d
−yx2ex/yi+xy2ex/yj
e
1−yx2yex/yi+x−1xy2ex/yj
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we find the partial derivatives: fx(x,y)=∂∂x(yxex/y)=(−yx2+yx⋅1y)ex/y=x−yx2ex/yfy(x,y)=∂∂y(yxex/y)=(1x−yx⋅xy2)ex/y=y−xxyex/y

Question 3
?

Given f(x,y)=3x+2yx−y, find ∇f(x,y).

a
 −5 (x i−y j)
b
 −5(x−y)2 (x i−y j)
c
 5(x−y)2 (y i+x j)
d
 −5 (y i−x j)
e
 −5(x−y)2 (y i−x j)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the partial derivatives: fx(x,y)=∂∂x(3x+2yx−y)=3(x−y)−(3x+2y)(x−y)2=−5y(x−y)2fy(x,y)=∂∂y(3x+2yx−y)=2(x−y)+(3x+2y)(x−y)2=5x(x−y)2

Hence, the gradient is:

∇f(x,y)=fx(x,y) i+fy(x,y) j=−5y(x−y)2 i+5x(x−y)2 j=−5(x−y)2 (y i−x j)

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\sqrt{y+3}) \\  & =2x\sqrt{y+3} \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}\sqrt{y+3}) \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2\sqrt{y+3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the gradient is:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨{f}_{x}(x,y),\,{f}_{y}(x,y)⟩ \\  & =⟨2x\sqrt{y+3},\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{2\sqrt{y+3}}⟩ \\ ∇f(2,1) & =⟨2\cdot 2\sqrt{1+3},\,\frac{{2}^{2}}{2\sqrt{1+3}}⟩ \\  & =⟨8,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Evaluate ∇f(x,y) at (2,1) if f(x,y)=x2y+3.

a
 ⟨16,1⟩
b
 ⟨2,0⟩
c
 ⟨8,1⟩
d
 ⟨1,8⟩
e
 ⟨4,12⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we find the partial derivatives:

fx(x,y)=∂∂x(x2y+3)=2xy+3fy(x,y)=∂∂y(x2y+3)=x22y+3. Hence, the gradient is:

∇f(x,y)=⟨fx(x,y),fy(x,y)⟩=⟨2xy+3,x22y+3⟩∇f(2,1)=⟨2⋅21+3,2221+3⟩=⟨8,1⟩

q-36005.name: Question 5
q-36005.worked_solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4x\operatorname{arctan}⁡y) \\  & =4\operatorname{arctan}⁡y \\ {h}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4x\operatorname{arctan}⁡y) \\  & =\frac{4x}{{y}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the gradient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇h(x,y) & =⟨{h}_{x}(x,y),\,{h}_{y}(x,y)⟩ \\  & =⟨4\operatorname{arctan}⁡y,\,\frac{4x}{{y}^{2}+1}⟩ \\ ∇h(1,1) & =⟨4\operatorname{arctan}⁡1,\,\frac{4\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+1}⟩ \\  & =⟨4\cdot \frac{\pi }{4},\,\frac{4}{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\pi ,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

q-35989.name: Question 6
q-35989.worked_solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{2xz}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}-1)) \\  & =2z{e}^{2xz}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}-1) \\ {g}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{2xz}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}-1)) \\  & =2y{e}^{2xz}\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{2}-1) \\ {g}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{2xz}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}-1)) \\  & =2x{e}^{2xz}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the gradient is: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & ={g}_{x}(x,y,z)\text{ }i+{g}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{g}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =2z{e}^{2xz}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}-1)\text{ }i+2y{e}^{2xz}\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{2}-1)\text{ }j+2x{e}^{2xz}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}-1)\text{ }k \\  & =2{e}^{2xz}\text{ }(z\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}-1)i+y\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{2}-1)\text{ }j+x\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2}-1)\text{ }k)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Given g(x,y,z)=e2xzsin⁡(y2−1), find ∇g(x,y,z).

a
 2e2xz (zi+y j+x k)
b
 2e2xz (zi+ycos⁡(y2−1) j+x k)
c
 2e2xz (zsin⁡(y2−1)i+ycos⁡(y2−1) j+xsin⁡(y2−1) k)
d
 zsin⁡(y2−1)i+ycos⁡(y2−1) j+xsin⁡(y2−1) k
e
 2e2xzsin⁡(y2−1) (zi+y j+x k)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we find the partial derivatives:

gx(x,y,z)=∂∂x(e2xzsin⁡(y2−1))=2ze2xzsin⁡(y2−1)gy(x,y,z)=∂∂y(e2xzsin⁡(y2−1))=2ye2xzcos⁡(y2−1)gz(x,y,z)=∂∂z(e2xzsin⁡(y2−1))=2xe2xzsin⁡(y2−1).

Hence, the gradient is: ∇g(x,y,z)=gx(x,y,z) i+gy(x,y,z) j+gz(x,y,z) k=2ze2xzsin⁡(y2−1) i+2ye2xzcos⁡(y2−1) j+2xe2xzsin⁡(y2−1) k=2e2xz (zsin⁡(y2−1)i+ycos⁡(y2−1) j+xsin⁡(y2−1) k)

Find ∇f(x,y,z), given that f(x,y,z)=1(x2+y2+z2)1/2.

a
 −1(x2+y2+z2)1/2(x2i+y2j+z2k)
b
1(x2+y2+z2)1/2(xi+yj+zk)
c
 1(x2+y2+z2)3/2(x2i+y2j+z2k)
d
2(x2+y2+z2)3/2(xi+yj+zk)
e
−1(x2+y2+z2)3/2(xi+yj+zk)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the partial derivatives:

fx(x,y,z)=∂∂x(1x2+y2+z2)=−x(x2+y2+z2)3/2fy(x,y,z)=∂∂y(1x2+y2+z2)=−y(x2+y2+z2)3/2fz(x,y,z)=∂∂z(1x2+y2+z2)=−z(x2+y2+z2)3/2.

Hence, the gradient is ∇f(x,y,z)=fx(x,y,z) i+fy(x,y,z) j+fz(x,y,z) k=(−x(x2+y2+z2)3/2)i+(−y(x2+y2+z2)3/2)j+(−z(x2+y2+z2)3/2)k=−1(x2+y2+z2)3/2(xi+yj+zk)

q-127945.name: Question 8
q-127945.worked_solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{y}+{y}^{z}) \\  & =y{x}^{y-1} \\ {f}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{y}+{y}^{z}) \\  & ={x}^{y}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+z{y}^{z-1} \\ {f}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{y}+{y}^{z}) \\  & ={y}^{z}\operatorname{ln}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =y{x}^{y-1}\,i+({x}^{y}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+z{y}^{z-1})j+{y}^{z}\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

If f(x,y,z)=xy+yz, find ∇f(x,y,z).

a
yxy−1i+zyz−1j+yzln⁡yk
b
(xyln⁡x+zyz−1)i+xyln⁡yj+yzln⁡zk
c
xyln⁡yi+xyln⁡xj+(xyln⁡x+zyz−1)k
d
yxy−1i+zyz−1j+zyz−1k
e
 yxy−1i+(xyln⁡x+zyz−1)j+yzln⁡yk
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we find the partial derivatives: fx(x,y,z)=∂∂x(xy+yz)=yxy−1fy(x,y,z)=∂∂y(xy+yz)=xyln⁡x+zyz−1fz(x,y,z)=∂∂z(xy+yz)=yzln⁡y

Hence, the gradient is ∇f(x,y,z)=fx(x,y,z)i+fy(x,y,z)j+fz(x,y,z)k=yxy−1i+(xyln⁡x+zyz−1)j+yzln⁡yk.

q-36968.name: Question 9
q-36968.worked_solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{x+2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{yz})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+2}}+0 \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+2}} \\ {g}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{x+2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{yz})) \\  & =0+\frac{1}{\sqrt{yz}}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{yz}}\cdot z \\  & =\frac{1}{2y} \\ {g}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\sqrt{x+2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{yz})) \\  & =0+\frac{1}{\sqrt{yz}}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{yz}}\cdot y \\  & =\frac{1}{2z}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,  the gradient is:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & ={g}_{x}(x,y,z)\text{ }i+{g}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{g}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+2}}i+\frac{1}{2y}\text{ }j+\frac{1}{2z}\text{ }k\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9

Find ∇g(x,y,z) given that g(x,y,z)=x+2+ln⁡(yz).

a
 12x+2i+12y j+12z k
b
 12x+2i+12yz j+12yz k
c
 12x+2i+12y j+12z k
d
 1x+2i+1yz j+1yz k
e
 1x+2i+1y j+1z k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the partial derivatives: gx(x,y,z)=∂∂x(x+2+ln⁡(yz))=12x+2+0=12x+2gy(x,y,z)=∂∂y(x+2+ln⁡(yz))=0+1yz⋅12yz⋅z=12ygz(x,y,z)=∂∂z(x+2+ln⁡(yz))=0+1yz⋅12yz⋅y=12z

Hence, the gradient is: ∇g(x,y,z)=gx(x,y,z) i+gy(x,y,z) j+gz(x,y,z) k=12x+2i+12y j+12z k
